summary: The flicker has two verified causes, plus a third that only shows in light mode. (1) Whenever the galaxy world's drawing buffer changes size outside a draw, one frame goes up blank. A quality governor level change is applied after the frame's draw (runtime.js:99-103 → gfx.setRatio → renderer.setPixelRatio/setSize → canvas.width/height). rt.resize (ResizeObserver) and rt.adopt resize without drawing at all. With preserveDrawingBuffer false and an alpha canvas, that frame is presented cleared: the planet, sky and ships vanish for one frame and the dark page background shows. Verified live on the real universe→galaxy entry: run3 at ?quality=high, DPR 2, governor fed a synthetic arrival clock. LEVEL 1 resized 640x360→408x229 inside the rAF after the draw, and screencast frame #45 has mean luminance 66.5 and 64% black, against 87 and 20-31% either side (run3_blank.png). The earlier attempt's forced runs agree: outB had 6/6 dark frames on size-changing setRatio/setSize, outA had none when the size was unchanged, outC had none when it redrew right after the resize. (2) The runtime and the WebGL backend fight over the pixel ratio. webgl.js:58-62 routes gfx.setSize through lib/three/renderer's fit(), which re-applies createRenderer's private budget ratio (renderer.js:51,56-59). That ratio is 2.0 at DPR 2 and 1.25 at DPR 1 on the high tier, and it ignores the runtime's quality ratio and the galaxy's 1.5 cap (gfx.js:32-36, runtime.js:178,197). Measured: after place() the renderer ran at 2.0 while gfx.ratio was 1.5 (canvas 640x360 for a 320x180 box). The first quality step then jumped 2.0→1.275, and any later resize jumps back to fit's ratio. So the picture changes sharpness 2→1.275→1.5 within seconds, and every alternation is a resize and a blank frame. It also makes post.js draw 4x MSAA half-float at 2x (post.js:217), which slows frames and trips the governor more. The governor (pace.js over quality.js) steps on arrival hitches and bounces back up. Fed into the real modules, a 60 Hz trace with 6 hitch frames in the first second gives L1 at 0.7 s and L0 at 5.2 s, i.e. 2 blank frames and 3 sharpness levels in 5 s. Borderline GPUs get down/up pairs 0.6 s apart, a double blink, repeating. quality.js:61-68 also floors for good 2.5 s after reaching the last step without checking the frames are still late, and quality.reset() is never called by the runtime. (3) Light-mode white flash at the hand-off. The universe page navigates on a fixed 1250 ms timer (Universe.jsx:205, flight.js:130). The hyperspace overlay runs on wall-clock time, is never held for the galaxy load, and vanishes at once when long main-thread tasks push it past T.end. The Galaxy page is not prefetched. The new page fades in from opacity 0 (.page-enter, index.css:834-835) over the light body #fdfdfc. Captured in 3 runs: screencast frames 94.9% near-white with the nav uncovered, then a 200-280 ms white→dark wash. With the Galaxy chunk delayed, the universe page reappeared for 2 s before the white wash. Dark mode hides the wash, but the overlay still cuts off abruptly. Refuted or not observed: z-fighting among sky layers (all depthWrite:false, pinned to the far plane), resize loops (no rt.resize on any entry), two scenes sharing one canvas, galaxy/tunnel.js (Death Star trench, unused here), exposure or bloom pulsing, and black or white first frames (first draw luminance was normal in every run). Headless runs at 2-3 fps and pace ignores gaps over 250 ms (pace.js:68), so the governor never fires naturally in headless; that is why the clock was synthetic. Scratch evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-new-portfolio-website/388c0198-4eb1-51a0-b00a-e0c292df4509/scratchpad/flicker2/ (entry2.mjs, entry3.mjs with the synthetic governor clock, entry4.mjs with the delayed chunk, lum.mjs; run1-run4 log.json and frames; run2_sheet.png, run3_sheet.png, run3_blank.png, run4_sheet.png) and in .../scratchpad/flicker/ (pace-sim.mjs, pace-sim2.mjs, run with node --import ./reg.mjs; force.mjs and outA/outB/outC). The repo was not modified, git status is clean, and the port 5191 server is stopped.

keyFiles.role: frame(): draw at 84-86, then quality.frame and gfx.setRatio at 99-103, so the resize lands after the draw and blanks the frame. backendFor 180-191 makes two backends on concurrent mounts (dev). build sets the ratio at 197; place() at 215-232 calls gfx.setSize at 230; resize at 271-276 and adopt at 386-400 never redraw.

setSize 27-31 and setRatio 32-36: setRatio sets the renderer ratio directly and writes the canvas twice (setPixelRatio, then setSize). The gfx.ratio getter reports the runtime's ratio, not the renderer's.
createRenderer gets budget.ratio at line 45. gfx.setSize is overridden at 58-62 to go through gl.setSize → fit(), which restores createRenderer's private ratio: one half of the ratio fight.

createRenderer: preserveDrawingBuffer false (39), checkShaderErrors in DEV (44), alpha clear 0 (49), private pixelRatio = maxRatio(budget) (51), fit() (56-59), setSize → fit (87-91). Shared with lib/three/useScene.
Governor wrapper. frame() at 48-71 floors permanently 2.5 s after reaching the last step, without checking lateness (61-68, against its header at 3-6). reset() at 72-78 has no production callers.

STEPS [1,.85,.72,.6,.5] (32). Gaps over 250 ms are ignored (68). Late threshold (77); 20-frame runs, 25% late → step down (90); 600 ms settle (99); hold doubles on a bounce (101); back up after 4 s clean (112).
ResizeObserver → rt.resize (70-71, runs after rAF, no redraw). Adopt before paint (41, 60). data-gl attribute (110-115).
fromScene('galaxy', …, { ratio: 1.5 }). The cap is ineffective while fit() overrides it.

camera near 0.05 / far 9000 (203); createPost (211); ratio follow via gfx.ratio (1755-1759); post.sharpness is read (1761) but never set; dust uses gfx.ratio (1881); resize/lowerQuality → sky.setRatio(gfx.ratio) (2197, 2231); ready waits for bake, warm and precompilePasses (2142); arrival 'exit' phase set on spawn (1780).

Composer shared by the universe map, the galaxy and the surfaces. MSAA samples fixed from the ratio at create time (217). sharpness API (262-272) can soften the scene without resizing the canvas. render() resizes its targets when the ratio changes (287-299).
Sky sphere and point layers: depthWrite false, pinned to the far plane (82, 189), renderOrder -20..-17 (rules out z-fighting). Star point size uses uDpr = gfx.ratio (186, 503-506).
go(): jumpEvent, then navigate(to) after a fixed plan.delay of 1250 ms (190-206). No prefetch of the galaxy and no hold on the overlay.
enterPlan: portal (Star Wars gate) → { mode: 'jump', delay: 1250 } (127-133).
Overlay runs on wall-clock time from its first frame (183-186). Ends at t ≥ T.end even if frames were starved (256-260). onPeak exists, but App's Lightspeed passes only onDone (App.jsx:116-119).
T timings (3). holdJump/holdStart (49-64) are used only for in-galaxy jumps (Galaxy.jsx:263).
3D overlay frame loop on the same wall-clock basis (308-311, 335-339).
Galaxy is lazy and never prefetched (31). page-enter wrapper keyed by page (325); pageKey keeps /galaxy/* as one page (288). Lightspeed mounts the overlay (86-121).
page-in fade 0.2 s from opacity 0 (834-835) over the light body (12, 366). .scene-canvas fades in on data-gl (904-905); .world-canvas has no such fade (runtime.css).
Intro shown once per session (128-134; masks the white flash on the first entry). Galaxy jumps hold the overlay (262-264). frozen during the intro (334).
useWorld(galaxyModule) (44). Loading line 'Plotting a course…' shown until status is 'on' (114-118).

Repro harness. Drives /universe/starwars → clicks .universe-enter, then logs every world draw (with read-back luminance), every canvas buffer reset with its stack, BLANK frames, setRatio/setSize/resize/adopt calls, LEVEL changes, long tasks, page-enter opacity and the overlay's lifetime, alongside a CDP screencast. SYNTH=1 feeds the governor a synthetic arrival clock.
Real quality.js and pace.js fed arrival frame-time traces E-I (run with node --import ./reg.mjs). pace-sim.mjs covers traces A-D.

rootCauses.title: Drawing-buffer resizes are presented undrawn: one blank frame at every quality step and every host resize
rootCauses.mechanism: runtime.js frame() draws the world (84-86), then calls quality.frame(t) and, on a level change, gfx.setRatio (99-103). That reaches renderer.setPixelRatio/setSize (gfx.js:32-36), which writes canvas.width/height and clears the WebGL drawing buffer after the frame's draw, within the same task. preserveDrawingBuffer is false (renderer.js:39) and the canvas is alpha with clear alpha 0 (renderer.js:49), so the compositor presents an empty canvas: the 3D picture disappears for a frame and the dark page background shows. rt.resize (runtime.js:271-276), called from the ResizeObserver after rAF callbacks (useWorld.js:70-71), and rt.adopt (runtime.js:396-397) resize without drawing, with the same effect. Writing the same size is harmless; only real size changes blank.
rootCauses.evidence: run3 (entry3.mjs, ?quality=high, DPR 2, 320x180, governor on a synthetic clock): LEVEL l=1 at frame 68, then 'reset' width 640→408 and height 360→229 with inRaf:true after that frame's draw, then BLANK frame 68. Screencast #45 at +30543 ms: mean 66.5, black 64.2%; neighbours #44 87.3/20.0% and #46 86.9/31.6%. run3_blank.png shows the planet and stars gone for one frame. Earlier force.mjs runs: outB had 6/6 size-changing setRatio/setSize events followed by a dark frame (means 23-27 vs 64-84, dark 83-88%); outA had none for 640→640; outC, which redrew right after each resize, had 0 dark frames in 6 trials.

rootCauses.title: Pixel-ratio fight: the WebGL backend's fit() undoes the runtime's quality ratio and the galaxy's 1.5 cap
rootCauses.mechanism: webgl.js:58-62 replaces gfx.setSize with lib/three/renderer's gl.setSize → fit() (renderer.js:56-59, 87-91). fit() re-applies createRenderer's private pixelRatio = maxRatio(budget.ratio) (renderer.js:51): 2 at DPR 2 and max(dpr,1.25) at DPR 1 on the high tier, max(dpr,1.5) on ultra. gfx.setRatio (gfx.js:32-36) sets the renderer directly but never updates that private value. So place() (runtime.js:230), rt.resize and adopt reset the ratio to the budget's, and every quality change jumps to quality.ratioUnder(1.5)×scale. The two alternate, each switch is a buffer resize (and a blank frame, see the first cause), and the sharpness jumps. gfx.ratio no longer matches the drawn ratio: stars, beacons, dust and world uniforms are sized for gfx.ratio (scene.js:1755-1759, 1881, 2197, 2231; sky.js:186, 503-506). post.js:217 picks MSAA samples from the renderer ratio at create time (1.5 → 4 samples) but then draws at 2.0, the expensive 4x half-float case its own comment warns against, so frames are slower and the governor steps more.
rootCauses.evidence: run3 (DPR 2, high): setSize(320,180) logged before 1.5 → after 2.0 with gfxRatio 1.5, canvas 640x360. The first LEVEL change logged setRatio r=1.275 before=2 (a 59% pixel cut in one frame). run2 (DPR 1, high): after place(), rRatio 1.25 while gfxRatio is 1, canvas 400x225 for a 320x180 box. outB: setSize after=1.25 when the runtime had set 1.0, so a resize undid the quality step. Sim E with this ratio path: 2.0 at mount → 1.275 at 0.7 s → 1.5 at 5.2 s.

rootCauses.title: The quality governor steps on arrival hitches, bounces, and can floor permanently
rootCauses.mechanism: pace.js judges 20-frame runs. If 25% or more are late (>max(1.5×beat, 20.8 ms)+1, line 77) it steps down (90), at least 600 ms apart (99). It steps back up after 4 s of clean frames (112) and doubles the wait when it bounces (101). The arrival (models.want plus warm/precompile, the war front streaming, stockUp) produces exactly such runs, so every entry can produce down/up pairs, each a resize, a blank frame and a sharpness pop. quality.js:61-68 floors (permanent scale 0.5, post.lite() bloom off, capDetail coarsest planets via lowerQuality) 2.5 s after reaching the last step, whether frames are still late or not. The header at 3-6 says it should only do so while they are. quality.reset() has no production callers, so the state carries across worlds.
rootCauses.evidence: Real quality.js and pace.js fed traces (pace-sim.mjs, pace-sim2.mjs). E (60 Hz, 8 ms frames, 6 hitches of 50-80 ms in the first second): 0.7 s→L1 (ratio 1.275), 5.2 s→L0 (1.5). B (20 ms at full): 7 changes in 60 s as pairs 0.6 s apart (4.7/5.3, 13.7/14.3, 30.3/31.0 s). C: 8 changes. A (bursts every 2.5 s for 12 s): L1-L4, floored at 10.6 s. D (30 fps cap): floored at 6.5 s. I (1 frame in 4 missing vsync): floored at 5.4 s. F (120 Hz) and G (3 hitches): 0. In headless it never fires naturally (2-3 fps, gaps over 250 ms ignored at pace.js:68); in run1 and run2 level stayed 0 throughout.

rootCauses.title: Hand-off timing: the overlay can end before or while the galaxy page fades in from opacity 0 over the light body (white flash in light mode)
rootCauses.mechanism: Universe go() navigates after a fixed 1250 ms from the click (Universe.jsx:205; flight.js:130), not on the overlay's onPeak (App.jsx:116-119 passes only onDone). The overlay's clock is wall time from its first frame (Hyperspace.jsx:183-186; hyperspace3d/scene.js:308-311). When long main-thread tasks starve it (3D jump context and compile setup, Galaxy chunk evaluation, runtime backend, scene.create; worse in dev with checkShaderErrors at renderer.js:44 and StrictMode), its next frame is past T.end and it removes itself without the tunnel and clear-out (Hyperspace.jsx:256-260). Nothing holds it for the galaxy (holdJump is used only for in-galaxy jumps, Galaxy.jsx:263). The Galaxy chunk is not prefetched (App.jsx:31). react-router 7.18.4's HashRouter navigates in startTransition, so the universe page stays up until the chunk arrives. The new page then mounts inside .page-enter (App.jsx:325) with page-in from opacity 0 over 0.2 s (index.css:834-835) on top of the light body #fdfdfc (index.html:2,39; index.css:12,366).
rootCauses.evidence: run2 screencast #6 at +6685 ms: mean 247.8, 94.9% near-white with the nav pill uncovered (the overlay is gone), then frames #7-#17 wash white→dark over ~280 ms (run2_sheet.png). run3 #6 at +7443 ms is identical. run3 log: overlay canvas removed at +7486 while .page-enter opacity was 0.378; page-in's startTime was only set after a 2479 ms long task starting at +4931. run4 (Galaxy.jsx delayed 4 s): overlay ended at +6485, the universe page was visible again until +8523, then the galaxy faded in from white (#9 at +8548: 87.4% white). Dark mode (body #09090b) hides the wash but not the abrupt overlay cut. The first entry per session is masked by GalaxyIntro (fixed, z 70, black; galaxy.css:406-413).

rootCauses.title: World canvas pops in after a dark loading gap (not flicker, but a hard cut)
rootCauses.mechanism: .world-canvas has no fade (runtime.css), unlike .scene-canvas (index.css:904-905). After the overlay ends the page shows 'Plotting a course…' (GalaxyView.jsx:114-118) until the first draw, then the scene appears mid-'exit' phase (scene.js:1780). The canvas is also inserted and sized one frame before its first draw (runtime.js:215-240); that frame is transparent, which is invisible because the background matches.
rootCauses.evidence: run1: ready at +4066, first draw at +10128. run2: +7320 → +13092. run3: +8036 → +13963 (headless SwiftShader; real GPUs are faster). BLANK logged at the place() frame in every run. The loading line is removed at the first draw.

rootCauses.title: Dev-only: StrictMode double mount builds two WebGL backends and leaks one
rootCauses.mechanism: Two concurrent rt.mount calls both reach backendFor (runtime.js:180-191) while gfx is still null, so makeBackend runs twice. The second assignment overwrites the first without dispose. Together with synchronous shader-error checks in DEV this lengthens the main-thread stalls that starve the overlay.
rootCauses.evidence: Two distinct gfx objects were logged on every entry: run1 at +3416/+3515, run2 at +6657/+6714, run3 at +7410/+7468. StrictMode is on (main.jsx:1,17).

proposals.title: Apply the quality level before the draw
proposals.description: In src/runtime/runtime.js frame(), move `const level = quality.frame(t); if (level !== null) { gfx.setRatio(ratioFor(current.module)); world.lowerQuality?.(level); }` (now 99-103) above `input.sample` / world.step / world.draw (83-86). Keep the snapshot block (92-98) after the draw. The governor only needs the frame's timestamp, so nothing depends on the draw having happened, and every ratio change is then followed by a draw in the same task.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: a world whose draw and lowerQuality, and a gfx whose setRatio, push to a shared order array; with quality.frame returning 1 on a tick, expect order ['setRatio','lowerQuality','draw']. The existing 'a new quality level sets the ratio and tells the world' and module-cap tests (317-337) must still pass.

proposals.title: Never leave a resized buffer undrawn: redraw in rt.resize and rt.adopt
proposals.description: In runtime.js resize() (271-276), after gfx.setSize and world.resize, draw the current world once at the new size when not inside a frame: world.draw({ dt: 0, now: last || performance.now(), renderer: gfx.renderer, quality }) with no step and no quality.frame, guarded by try/fail like frame(). adopt() reaches this through this.resize. This is the fix outC verified (0 dark frames in 6 trials vs 6/6 without). Alternative: store a pending size and apply it at the start of the next frame(), before the draw, which gives one stretched frame instead of a blank one.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: mount, then rt.resize(800,450) → gfx.setSize(800,450), world.resize(800,450), then world.draw called once with dt 0 in that order, and step not called. With no current world, nothing is drawn.

proposals.title: One owner of the pixel ratio
proposals.description: Have gfx.js apply ratio and size together: keep `size` and `ratio`; both setSize(w,h) and setRatio(r) call apply(), which runs renderer.setPixelRatio(fit(size.w,size.h,ratio)) then renderer.setSize(size.w,size.h,false), and skips both when the resulting floor(w*r)×floor(h*r) buffer is unchanged. makeGfx takes an optional fit (default identity). In webgl.js drop the setSize override (58-62) and pass `fit: (w,h,r) => fitRatio(w,h,r,{ side: maxSide(renderer) })` (both exported from lib/three/renderer). Do not change createRenderer's own fit()/watchdog: useScene pages rely on them. Then gfx.ratio equals the drawn ratio (unless the chip limit cuts it), the galaxy's 1.5 cap holds from the first frame, resizes no longer undo quality steps, and post.js:217's sample choice matches what is drawn.
proposals.tests: New src/runtime/gfx.test.js with a fake renderer that records setPixelRatio/setSize and a fake canvas: setRatio(1.5) then setSize(320,180) → last pixel ratio 1.5 and buffer 480x270; setSize(320,180) again → no renderer calls; setRatio(1.275) → 408x229 buffer; a fit that caps at side 4096 is honoured.

proposals.title: Soften the galaxy through its post composer instead of resizing the canvas
proposals.description: Add a module option (for example fromScene(..., { ratio: 1.5, soften: 'post' }), runtime/module.js:43-50) under which runtime.js frame() keeps gfx at ratioFor(module) with scale 1 and passes the scale to the world: world.setScale?.(quality.scale), or lowerQuality(level) with STEPS[level] read by the scene. In galaxy scene.js lowerQuality (2230-2236), set post.sharpness = STEPS[Math.min(level, STEPS.length-1)]. post.js already renders the scene at renderer ratio × sharp and stretches it over a canvas that keeps its size, so the HUD stays crisp (post.js:19-22, 262-272, 287-299). This removes canvas resizes for quality changes entirely. The scene already reads post.sharpness for planet detail (scene.js:1761).
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: a module with soften:'post', quality.frame → 2 → gfx.setRatio not called with a scaled ratio, and world.lowerQuality(2) or setScale(0.72) called. post.test.js: setting sharpness to 0.72 changes the composer's pixel ratio on the next render() but not renderer.getPixelRatio().

proposals.title: Governor warm-up after a world starts, and a floor that requires late frames
proposals.description: (a) In runtime.js begin() (233-240) call quality.reset?.() and quality.hold?.(3000), a new quality.js method that ignores frames until the first frame time + 3000 ms, so arrival streaming (models, war front, stockUp) cannot step the level. (b) In quality.js frame(), floor only when the pace reports it is stuck at its softest step with frames still late: expose pace.stuck, or count via pace's onFloor at pace.js:92-97, instead of the plain 2.5 s timer at quality.js:61-68. Optionally require two consecutive bad runs before the first step down from level 0.
proposals.tests: quality.test.js: after hold(3000), late frames within 3 s never change the level, and the same frames after 3 s do. A fake pace sitting at the last level but not stuck never floors; once it reports stuck it floors once. The existing 'floors once when the last step still misses' test (53-74) must have its fake pace report stuck. Re-run the scratch pace-sim2 traces A-I as table tests: E must give 0 changes in the first 3 s.

proposals.title: Hold the jump until the galaxy is drawing, keep the overlay's clock from leaping, and prefetch
proposals.description: (1) timeline.js: add a pure clampStart(start, lastNow, now, maxStep = 50) → start + max(0, now - lastNow - maxStep), and use it in both frame loops (Hyperspace.jsx:184-186 and hyperspace3d/scene.js:309-311). A starved overlay then pauses instead of skipping its tunnel and clear-out. (2) Universe.jsx go(): when the target starts with '/galaxy' and mode is 'jump', take `const letGo = holdJump(8000)` (timeline.js:52) and hand it over, e.g. a module-level pending hold in timeline.js that GalaxyView (or useWorld's status effect) releases the first time status becomes 'on', 'failed' or 'lost'. The tunnel then covers the whole load and clears onto a drawing galaxy. (3) Prefetch when Star Wars is selected or the jump starts: import('../pages/Galaxy') and import('../components/galaxy/scene') (as prefetchSurface does, travel.js:44). (4) Stop the light body showing under world pages: `.page-enter:has(.universe-page) { animation: none; }`, or html:has(.universe-page) { background: #03040a }.
proposals.tests: timeline.test.js: clampStart leaves normal 16 ms frames alone and absorbs a 2 s gap down to 50 ms. A hold taken before the galaxy mounts keeps holdStart at HOLD_AT until released and is released by its timeout. Browser check: the scratch entry4.mjs (DELAY=4000) and entry3.mjs should show no frame with more than 50% near-white pixels and the overlay canvas removed only after status 'on'.

proposals.title: Fade the world canvas in on its first frame
proposals.description: Add `.world-host[data-gl='loading'] > .world-canvas { opacity: 0; } .world-canvas { transition: opacity 0.4s var(--ease-out); }` to runtime.css, matching .scene-canvas (index.css:904-905). Use only the 'loading' selector so adopted or handed-over worlds, which arrive already 'on' with a snapshot cover, are untouched. This hides the transparent place() frame and turns the pop-in into a fade.
proposals.tests: No Vitest (CSS only). Browser check with the scratch harness: luminance across the first draw rises over about 0.4 s instead of in one frame. scripts/galaxy-check.mjs still passes.

proposals.title: Share one pending backend between concurrent mounts
proposals.description: In runtime.js backendFor (180-191), keep `making = makeBackend(...)` as a promise per kind and await it, so a second mount while the first is still creating reuses the same backend instead of creating and leaking another WebGL context. This only bites under dev StrictMode or rapid remounts.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: makeBackend returns a deferred promise; call rt.mount twice before resolving, resolve, flush → makeBackend called once and rt.gfx is that backend.

constraints: src/runtime is tested in Node with the browser parts injected (runtime.js:7-8, runtime.test.js fakes for backend, loop, quality and world). Keep frame ordering and resize behaviour expressible with those fakes.
runtime.test.js:317-337 pins that a level change calls gfx.setRatio(quality ratio or ratioUnder(cap)) and world.lowerQuality(level), and that a module's ratio caps the sharpness.

quality.test.js:53-74 pins the floor behaviour with a fake pace that never reports lateness. Changing the floor rule means updating that fake. pace.test.js pins pace's step, settle and hold behaviour.

lib/three/renderer.js createRenderer, fit() and watchdog are shared by lib/three/useScene (the universe map and other pages); renderer.test.js pins fitRatio and watchdog. Fix the fight in runtime/gfx.js and webgl.js, not in createRenderer.
universe/post.js is shared by the universe map, the galaxy and its surfaces. Keep the sharpness, ratio and samples semantics and post.test.js passing.
Handover covers depend on the snapshot being taken right after the draw in the same task (runtime.js:92-98). Any reordering must keep takeSnap after world.draw.

Headless Chromium on SwiftShader runs at 2-3 fps here, so pace never judges naturally (gaps over 250 ms are ignored, pace.js:68). Browser verification of governor behaviour needs a synthetic clock, as entry3.mjs SYNTH=1 does.
Same-size canvas.width writes did not blank in Chrome (outA). Only real size changes need the redraw.
Light mode is the default (index.html:2). Dark mode hides the white wash, so verify any fix for the hand-off flash in light mode.

This was a read-only investigation: no tracked files were edited and nothing was committed. Scratch files are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-new-portfolio-website/388c0198-4eb1-51a0-b00a-e0c292df4509/scratchpad/flicker2 and .../flicker.
openQuestions: Is the owner in light or dark mode, and on the dev server or a production build? Light mode plus dev (StrictMode, synchronous shader checks, unbundled modules) makes the white hand-off flash likely. In dark mode the visible flicker is mostly the blank frames at quality steps.
What are the owner's display DPR and GPU? At DPR 2 the ratio fight is 2.0 vs 1.5×scale. On an ultra-detail card at DPR 1 it is 1.5 vs 1.0.

What does the real arrival frame-time trace look like? SwiftShader cannot give one. Logging LEVEL events on the owner's machine with entry3.mjs-style hooks, or a 30 s Performance trace, would confirm how often the governor steps in the first seconds; the sims show 0-2 steps for a strong GPU and repeated down/up pairs for a borderline one.

Should the galaxy's 1.5 cap stay? It never takes effect today because fit() restores the budget ratio (2.0 at DPR 2). Fixing the fight lowers the galaxy's default sharpness on retina screens, which is cheaper but visibly softer than what the owner sees now.

Unverified secondary shimmer: sky stars are hard 1-px point sprites (sky.js:186, size clamped to at least 1 device px) and may twinkle during the arrival FOV zoom (scene.js:1820). Separately, with camera near 0.05 / far 9000 (scene.js:203), 24-bit depth steps exceed 1 unit beyond about 1000 units, so far capital ships' coplanar detail could z-fight. Neither showed up in these runs.
